veranderings.rede: 'Soos as' is spoken and clumsy in written text; 'soos wanneer' is the natural written form with the same meaning.

veranderings.blok: Ook vir iemand wat jy ken
veranderings.rede: A list of three verbs reads more smoothly with a comma than with a repeated 'en'; the meaning is unchanged.

veranderings.blok: By die kliniek en die dokter
veranderings.voor: vra dan jou en die grootmens by jou
veranderings.na: vra dan vir jou en vir die grootmens by jou
veranderings.rede: With two people as the object of 'vra', 'vir' before each is the natural Afrikaans construction and avoids the stiff 'vra dan jou'.

veranderings.voor: Sê dit vir nog een as daardie grootmens nie help nie
veranderings.na: Sê dit vir nog 'n grootmens as die eerste een nie help nie
veranderings.rede: Naming the noun first makes it clear at once that 'nog een' means another adult; the condition is unchanged.

veranderings.blok: As niemand naby jou help nie
veranderings.voor: Jy bel 116 enige tyd van die dag of die nag.
veranderings.na: Jy kan 116 enige tyd van die dag of die nag bel.
veranderings.rede: The bare present 'Jy bel 116' reads like a report rather than telling the child it is possible; 'Jy kan ... bel' is the natural form and still says the child phones herself.

veranderings.na: Vra daarom voordat jy aan hom raak.
veranderings.rede: 'Aanraak' needs an object; 'aan hom raak' points back to 'iemand anders' in the sentence before.

vlae.teks: Medisyne is 'n middel wat help om siekte of pyn te behandel.
vlae.rede: The study sentence leaves out the second half of the decided shared definition of medisyne ('of om te keer dat 'n mens siek word'), which the lesson's own glossary entry has. Whether that is deliberate is a content question, not a language one, so this is not proposed as a change.
